text:
Incident Bot: paging @sre oncall — p99 latency spike detected for streaming endpoints in us-west-2, ongoing for ~6m, clients reporting stalled chunks :rotating_light:

sre-alex: seeing the alert, grabbing traces now. p95 also rising. which customers showing errors?

support-olivia: customer-svc-42 (chat API) opened a ticket, says messages stop arriving mid-stream. attaching logs they sent.

runtime-maria: from traces: proxy->runtime queue depth shoots up, then proxies start returning 202 with no body for ~200ms windows. Looks like client backpressure + connection write stalls.

eng-raj: any recent deploys to streaming proxy or runtime in the last hour?

oncall-bot: recent deploys: runtime v3.14.2 (10:12 UTC), streaming-proxy v1.8.0 (10:05 UTC). No rollbacks.

devon: I rolled the streaming-proxy canary at 10:05 but kept it at 5% — could still be correlated. Will check proxy metrics.

prodops-lee: net infra shows no AZ flapping. Network egress to us-west-2 GPU cluster stable.

sre-alex: collecting p99 by route: /v1/stream/chat p99 = 1.9s (baseline 350ms), p95 = 540ms. Tail latency distribution looks bimodal.

runtime-maria: dump of socket stats from runtime nodes (snip):
```
TASK backlog: 120 -> 170
KV cache miss rate: 4.2%
client write buffer backlog: 78% -> 98% on nodes rt-3, rt-4
```

eng-raj: client write buffer hitting 98% suggests slow consumers. Could be a burst of large responses + small client read window. Any change to chunk sizes?

devon: no config changes to chunking. But I see an increase in tail token counts per request (users sending longer prompts) starting ~10:07.

support-olivia: one customer says they see a sequence of empty stream events then finally the last token comes through. Might match the 200ms silence windows.

sre-alex: mitigation idea: enable immediate proxy flush on chunk boundaries for affected routes to avoid coalescing, and temporarily relax keepalive to ensure sockets aren't GC'd. Can someone toggle proxy flush for /v1/stream/chat?

eng-raj: I can flip a config flag on the canary pool and roll to 20% if that helps. Plan: flip flush_on_chunk=true on canary proxies, monitor p99 for 5m, then expand.

runtime-maria: also suggest reducing max batch window to avoid large batches holding up tail tokens: temp set max_batch_ms=10 on runtime pool. I can push that to dedicated runtime nodes.

devon: doing proxy flag now on canary group... flipping... :gear:

Incident Bot: config change applied to streaming-proxy canary (group proxy-canary-2).

sre-alex: seeing immediate drop in p95 to ~420ms and p99 down to 720ms on canary traffic. Good signal.

eng-raj: rolling canary to 40% now. Watch for errors.

support-olivia: notifying affected customers: sending note that we are investigating increased streaming stalls, temporary mitigation being rolled, ETA 15m for resolution.

prodops-lee: adding a circuit-breaker rule to limit per-client parallel streams at 8 to protect runtime. Pushing rule now.

oncall-bot: circuit-breaker rule deployed across edge proxies.

sre-alex: overall cluster p99 now 430ms, p95 360ms. We'll monitor for 10m. Need to assess whether to keep flush_on_chunk permanent or find underlying cause.

runtime-maria: logs show some client connections with tiny read windows causing TCP flow-control pauses; this amplifies when runtime batches bigger responses. The short-term fixes reduce tail risk but root cause likely a combination of larger responses + client-side slow reads.

eng-raj: follow-ups: add telemetry to capture per-connection read-rate and # of pending write bytes, improve alert rule to trigger earlier on write-buffer growth.

devon: will open a PR to add the telemetry and an alert threshold for write backlog > 60% sustained for 30s.

support-olivia: continuing to update customers. No escalations yet, CS asks estimated incident severity?

sre-alex: severity: SEV3 (partial degradation affecting multiple customers, degraded p99 but no total outage). We'll keep it open until p99 stabilizes under 500ms for 15m.

Incident Bot: paging next oncall @runtime team for handoff in 20m: @runtime-maria will hand over to @eng-raj if persists.

runtime-maria: I'll start a handoff doc in #incidents-postmortem and collect traces + affected customer IDs.

eng-raj: if this resurges after config rollback, we'll need a short playbook: 1) enable flush_on_chunk 2) lower batch window 3) apply per-client throttle 4) notify customers.

devon: noted. I'll keep canary at 40% for 30m then we can decide full rollout.

prodops-lee: tracking runbook items and will include capacity impact estimation for Dedicated customers.

support-olivia: closing loop with customer-svc-42 — they confirm better behaviour after the changes, will monitor.

sre-alex: monitoring looks stable for now. tagging this thread for post-incident review. Thanks all.

oncall-bot: reminder: handoff scheduled in 18 minutes.

Incident Bot: incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Postmortem owner: runtime-maria.
